title: JVM via JFR
description: Live JVM internals streamed from Java Flight Recorder via jfr2grafana-agent. One row per metric family; see panel descriptions for known platform caveats (macOS/aarch64 CPU ratios, sampled allocation estimate, contention-threshold gaps).

panels.title: Events processed/sec
panels.description: Rate of jfr2grafana_events_processed_total across all event types. Flat non-zero confirms the agent is alive and the RecordingStream is flowing.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Wall-clock time the agent's own /metrics scrape took to render.

panels.title: Events dropped/sec
panels.description: jdk event callbacks the engine discarded (e.g. filtered by threshold/period). 0 is expected most of the time.

panels.title: Cardinality drops/sec
panels.description: Label combinations collapsed into __other__ after a metric's maxCardinality cap was exceeded (e.g. per-thread CPU, per-class allocation/lock labels). 0 is expected in a light POC workload.

panels.title: Heap occupancy
panels.description: Sampled after each GC (jdk.GCHeapSummary, when="After GC").

panels.title: Metaspace occupancy
panels.description: Sampled after each GC (jdk.MetaspaceSummary, when="After GC").

panels.title: Fraction of time paused for GC
panels.description: rate() of cumulative GC-pause seconds: seconds paused per wall-clock second.

panels.title: GC phase pause duration (p99 by phase)
Allocation rate by class (ESTIMATE — sampled event)
panels.description: jfr_allocation_bytes_total is derived from jdk.ObjectAllocationSample's sampled `weight` field, not an exact per-allocation byte count. Treat this as a statistically reasonable estimate of allocation pressure, not a precise measurement.

panels.title: CPU utilization (lead with machine total)
panels.description: jfr_cpu_jvm_user_ratio / jfr_cpu_jvm_system_ratio read a flat 0.0 on macOS/aarch64 hosts (JDK/OS quirk, not a bug) — jfr_cpu_machine_total_ratio populates on every platform and is the series to trust for "is this JVM using CPU". Inside the Linux docker-compose container the JVM-specific series are expected to populate normally.

panels.title: Thread creation rate
panels.description: rate() of the JVM's cumulative jdk.JavaThreadStatistics.accumulatedCount (mapped as counter_absolute).

panels.title: Per-thread CPU (top 10, capped at 20 distinct threads)
panels.description: jdk.ThreadCPULoad is capped at maxCardinality=20; thread names beyond the cap collapse into thread="__other__".

panels.title: Monitor blocked time (p50 / p99)
panels.description: Only synchronized-monitor acquisitions blocked ≥1ms are recorded. No data is expected while the app is idle or under /load/contend hasn't been driven — that is correct behaviour, not a broken panel.

panels.title: Monitor blocked time heatmap
panels.description: Populates once contention above the 1ms threshold occurs — drive /load/contend on the sample app to see it fill in.

panels.title: Monitor wait time (p99, by timeout)
panels.description: Object.wait() calls lasting ≥1ms. No data when the workload never waits — expected.

panels.title: Thread park time (p99)
panels.description: LockSupport.park/parkNanos calls lasting ≥1ms (e.g. idle pool workers, blocking-queue waits).

panels.title: Safepoint pause duration (p99)
panels.description: Every JVM safepoint pause is recorded regardless of duration — unlike lock events there is no threshold.

panels.title: Compiler bailouts & bytes compiled
panels.description: Bailouts on the left scale; bytes-compiled rates share the panel for a quick JIT-activity overview — see individual queries for exact units (bailouts=count/sec, bytes=bytes/sec).
